q: When you are stuck in this hat, what do you do next?
hint: The way out of the corner.

q: What should this hat never do for you, even when asked nicely?
hint: A hard never, in your words.

q: What do people expect from this hat that you refuse to give them?
hint: The thing you push back on.

q: What is the shortcut in this work that you will not take?
hint: The corner you refuse to cut.

q: When should you take this hat off and say it is not the right one for the job?
hint: The moment to hand it back.

q: What would embarrass you if this hat did it in your name?
hint: The worst version of it.

q: What has to be true before you give any advice in this hat?
hint: The condition it checks first.

q: What question do you ask before anything else when you wear it?
hint: The one you never skip.

q: When does this hat stop and hand the decision back to you?
hint: Where its authority ends.

q: Who should you never speak for while wearing this hat, and why?
hint: A line around other people.

q: What is the line you hold in this hat no matter who is asking?
hint: The rule that survives pressure.

q: How does your tone change when this hat is on?
hint: Warmer, sharper, slower, plainer.

q: Which words or phrases show up more when you wear it?
hint: The vocabulary of the hat.

q: Which sentence sounds most like you in this hat?
hint: Pick the one you would actually say.
options: Short and to the point.
Warm and a little playful.
Careful, every claim backed up.
Bold, and happy to be argued with.

q: How much do you explain your reasoning when you are wearing it?
hint: All of it, the gist, or just the call.

q: What does this hat sound like when it disagrees with you?
hint: The tone of its pushback.
